items.caption:
POV: the day after a sleepless night.
In one 2007 brain-scan experiment with healthy young adults, staying awake about 35 hours left the amygdala (the brain's alarm centre) about 60% more reactive to upsetting pictures than after a normal night, with a weaker link to the front of the brain. A 2020 study linked more deep sleep to lower anxiety the next day. Small studies of healthy adults, and the deep-sleep result is a link, not proof. If it keeps costing you sleep, talk to a doctor.
